advisories.title: php2shell: unauthenticated remote code execution in the PHP runtime
advisories.summary: Two memory-safety flaws in the PHP interpreter itself (out-of-memory request corruption and stale request state use-after-free) allow unauthenticated remote code execution and worker memory disclosure on every PHP installation serving web requests (mod_php, PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed). Application code changes cannot fix them: the PHP runtime must be upgraded and every PHP process restarted.
actions: Upgrade every PHP runtime to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 (or your vendor's patched build), prioritising internet-facing and mod_php systems.
Restart Apache, PHP-FPM and all long-running PHP workers after upgrading; updating WordPress/Drupal/your app does not update the PHP runtime.
Inventory PHP everywhere: containers, bundled runtimes, control panels and vendor appliances (PHP is often an invisible component).
PHP 8.1 and older receive no official fix: move to a supported branch or an LTS vendor backport.
If you cannot patch immediately, NSA, CISA and NCSC advise taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated. A WAF only provides partial protection.

Temporary measures only (not a fix): session.upload_progress.enabled=0 (and fatal_error_backtraces=0 on 8.5) in php.ini / FPM pool / server config, not ini_set() or .user.ini; memory_limit=-1 set so apps cannot override it; low post_max_size and proxy request-size limits. Never use RLIMIT_AS / RLIMIT_DATA as a substitute.
Check for compromise before and after patching: look for web shells and modified files, and monitor PHP workers spawning shells or downloading tools.
Rotate credentials, tokens, API keys and certificates held by PHP applications that were exposed before patching, because CVE-2026-109619 can leak worker memory without executing code.
